faq.subtitle: OKR method, habits, time-blocking, demo mode, security... we answer everything.
faq.a1: Yes. Every core feature — tasks, habits, calendar, OKRs and statistics — is completely free. Premium access (team collaboration, task sharing) is earned by watching a short ad, without ever reaching for your card.
faq.q2: What is the OKR method and why use it?
faq.a2: The OKR method (Objectives & Key Results) is the goal-setting system used by Google, Intel and Netflix. One OKR = one ambitious qualitative objective + 2 to 5 measurable key results. Cosmo computes progress for you and shows where you stand in real time, with no spreadsheet.
faq.q3: How is it different from Notion or Todoist?
faq.a3: Notion is a very flexible notes space, but with no built-in productivity structure. Todoist is an excellent task manager, but it doesn't cover habits, OKRs or time-blocking. Cosmo is the only app that connects all four pillars — tasks, habits, calendar and objectives — in one coherent ecosystem.
faq.a4: Click "Try the demo": you get the full app straight away, pre-filled with 100 tasks, 100 habits, 150 calendar events and 8 OKRs across 12 months of realistic data. No account, no email asked. When you're convinced, create your real account in 30 seconds.
faq.a5: Yes. Cosmo is built mobile-first: responsive interface, bottom navigation bar, swipe gestures on tasks, smooth bottom sheets and iOS safe-area support. It runs in any mobile browser — Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android — with nothing to download.
faq.a6: Time-blocking means reserving slots in your calendar to work on specific tasks, instead of reacting as things come. In Cosmo, just drag a task from the side panel onto a slot in your calendar: the event is created automatically and linked to the task. It's the method favoured by Elon Musk, Bill Gates and Cal Newport.
faq.q7: Can I collaborate with my team?
faq.a7: Yes. With Premium access (free via an ad), send friend requests by email, share tasks with a Viewer or Editor role, and follow your collaborators' progress from your dashboard. Contextual messaging lets you discuss right inside a task.
faq.q8: How do I track my habits effectively?
faq.a8: Create a habit, set its frequency (daily, weekly, specific days), then tick it off each day. Cosmo shows a GitHub-style 26-week heatmap, computes your streak (consecutive days) and your completion rate over the period you choose. The golden rule: start with 2 to 3 habits at most.
faq.a9: Your data is stored on Supabase with Row Level Security: nobody else can reach your tasks or habits. The app's pages (dashboard, tasks, etc.) are blocked for search crawlers in robots.txt. In demo mode, data stays in your browser (localStorage) and never touches our servers.
faq.q10: Can I use Cosmo without an internet connection?
faq.a10: In demo mode, all data is stored locally in your browser — no connection needed after the initial load. With an account, a 24-hour localStorage cache lets you consult your recent tasks and habits even on a shaky connection.

about.title: About Cosmo
about.subtitle: A free, all-in-one productivity app.
about.p1: Getting organised in 2026 too often looks like this: a to-do list somewhere, a habits app elsewhere, a calendar in a third tool, and new-year objectives… in a spreadsheet nobody opens again. Each tool is fine, but none of them talk to each other.
about.p2before: Cosmo starts from a simple conviction:
about.p2bold: personal productivity rests on four pillars — tasks, habits, time and objectives
about.p2after: — and they only really work when connected. A task gets scheduled in the calendar, a habit feeds an objective, and all of it is measured in one place.
about.principle1: The core features are free, with no artificial limits. We would rather convince you than lock you in.
about.principle2: The demo opens with no account and no email, pre-filled with 12 months of realistic data. Judge for yourself.
about.principle3: Tasks, habits, calendar and objectives are designed together from the start — not bolted on afterwards.
about.principle4: Secure storage with Row Level Security, and in demo mode nothing leaves your browser.
about.namesP: All three refer to the same app:
about.namesAfter: . People also look for us as “Cosmo app”, “The Cosmo” or “thecosmo app” — it's always us. Not to be confused with other products of the same name on mobile stores: Cosmo is a web app, with nothing to download, and its only official site is thecosmo.app.
about.whoP: Cosmo is an independent product, built in France by a very small team — no funding round, no aggressive growth hacking, just a product we improve every week by listening to what users tell us.
